proposals.relationship: Davis praises The Birth of Purgatory but asks for more rigorous causal links between its cultural parallels, especially cartography and judicial practice (1985).

proposals.relationship: While accepting Le Goff’s medieval cultural turning point, Ariès argues that his focus on purgatory as a place understates enduring older beliefs in repose and waiting (1983).
proposals.evidence_note: Printed pp. 153–156. Ariès accepts the terminus ad quem and cultural significance. His diffusion discussion allows regional variation and revises his own earlier late dating; this is no blanket denial of Le Goff’s thesis. French book (1981) not independently read.

proposals.relationship: Reviewing Moreira, Brown rejects the doctrinal-stagnation framing exemplified by Le Goff’s chapter heading and endorses continuing creative theological debate in the early Middle Ages (2012).
proposals.evidence_note: Brown names Le Goff, then states his own counterclaim in the Moreira discussion. Moreira’s contribution and her criticism of Brown’s earlier Irish-law explanation remain explicit. This is a scoped critical reception, not Brown’s independent refutation of every claim in the unread book.
primary_locators: “She dismisses this model firmly,” Brown’s own self-qualification.
